messages.content: what is distiller

**Playbook Distiller** is the auto-learning component of CRS Brain's "Playbook" system: after each turn/session, it analyzes what happened (successes, failures, error signatures) and distills a lesson into `crs-brain/data/playbook.json` — a structured store of operational rules (categories: platform-gotcha, cli-bug, workspace-rule, design-pattern, verification, decision-pointer), each with a trigger, rule, fix, error signature, hit count, and recurrence tracking.

The point: instead of you re-explaining the same gotcha every session, the distiller writes it down once, the system injects relevant lessons into future turns automatically, and if a mistake recurs despite the lesson being loaded, it flags that (recurrence alarm) rather than silently repeating.

Per `brain/qa/checkpoints/playbook.md`, this was verified end-to-end 2026-07-19 (store/migration, injection, recurrence alarm, toasts+ledger, playbook.html surface) — program is marked **CLOSED**, 216 checklist rows (204 PASS / 12 ENV-LIMITED / 0 FAIL).

messages.content: what is playbook and what is distiller

**Playbook** = the store itself: `crs-brain/data/playbook.json`, a list of operational lessons (as opposed to `memory.json`, which holds human/preference facts about you). Each entry has category (platform-gotcha, cli-bug, workspace-rule, design-pattern, verification, decision-pointer), trigger, rule, fix, error signature, hit count, last-hit, and recurred status. It's browsable/editable at `playbook.html` in the CRS Brain app.

**Distiller** = the process that writes to that store. After a turn/session runs, it looks at what happened — a caught error, a fix that worked, a mistake corrected — and "distills" it into a new playbook entry (or bumps hits on an existing one) so the same mistake doesn't need re-explaining next time.

How they connect: Distiller writes → Playbook stores → future turns get relevant lessons injected automatically ("Playbook check — N lessons loaded") → if a mistake happens again despite the lesson being loaded, a recurrence alarm fires (warning + todo), because that means the lesson didn't actually prevent anything.

Confirmed built and verified 2026-07-19 (`brain/qa/checkpoints/playbook.md`) — 7 seed lessons migrated from memory.json, prevention proven live (a planted mistake was actually avoided because the injected lesson blocked it). Program closed.

messages.content: what is ledger

"Ledger" isn't one single file — it's a pattern: several **append-only `.jsonl` logs** under `crs-brain/data/` that record events as they happen and are never edited/overwritten, only appended to. The ones referenced in this project:

- `learn-events.jsonl` — distiller output (lessons learned/applied/recurred), served by `/api/learn-events`
- `audit.jsonl` — mutation trail (who/what/when, incl. remote/desktop/scheduler origin), served by `/api/audit`
- `notifications`, `action-log`, `usage-log` — same append-only pattern for their respective domains

They exist so nothing gets silently overwritten — history stays inspectable even after autoCommit or probe cleanup sweeps the working files. On the Live System Map (`LIVEMAP.1`), "LEDGER" is literally a node in the diagram — PLAYBOOK/DISTILLER feeds into it, i.e. the distiller's output lands in the ledger.

- No changelog page exists publicly; recent news is just "Buildprint 2.0 alpha" (complete rebuild, ~March 2026) and an AI plugin-builder feature — nothing about visual workflows
- The one forum hit for "workflow visualization" was an unrelated third-party plugin request from the Bubble forum, not Buildprint

There's no evidence a visual workflow-diagram feature exists yet, in this CLI version (4.2.7) or on the website. What you may have seen could be:
- Bubble's own native workflow editor canvas (that's Bubble, not Buildprint)
- A Buildprint 2.0 alpha feature not yet public/documented

messages.content: check gmail for buildprint updates

Found it — **Buildprint Weekly Update #19** (2026-07-26) confirms this is real and new.

## What's new: Inline workflow visualisation
> "Buildprint will now show your logic in inline workflows. It will show it in a readable way, so that it makes understanding easier, without losing any precision."

## Key detail — where it lives
This is a **Buildprint web app / chat feature**, not a CLI command. The email explicitly frames it around users who "spend very little time in the Bubble editor, and more and more of it in Buildprint" — meaning the **Buildprint chat interface at buildprint.ai**, not the `buildprint` CLI I'm running here (v4.2.7, which has no `workflow` command, confirmed earlier).

So I can't render this inline-workflow view myself from this workspace/CLI session — it's a feature of the web chat UI, separate from the CLI tool I operate through.

## Other items in the same update (#19)
- **Better plans** — Buildprint plans now shown inline with affected app areas + step details, trackable progress
- **Agents can ask you questions** — inline clarifying questions from agents in chat
- **BubbleScript** (in internal testing) — a new TypeScript-like language replacing raw JSON for agent edits; faster, better validation, longer-horizon tasks, better UI-gen. Will roll out as an experimental workspace setting when stable
- Fixes: thread forking, unlimited conversation length, agent-stop bug (with auto credit refunds), added Opus 5 / Grok 4.5 model options, overage warning emails

**Next:** if you want to see the visual workflow view, that'd be through buildprint.ai's own chat/dashboard, not through me in this terminal session. Want me to keep watching for a CLI-side equivalent (`buildprint update` to check for a new version), or is the web view enough?
